title: QUIZ - 100
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the logical OR operator to a two-condition pass/fail scenario
questions.question: A student passes a course if their exam score is at least 75 OR they have completed at least 9 extra-credit assignments. A student has a score of 67 and completed 5 extra-credit assignments. Does the student pass?

options.label: A
options.text: The student passes only if both conditions are met.

options.label: B
options.text: This cannot be determined from the given information.

options.label: C
options.text: No, the student does not pass.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, the student passes.

questions.explanation: Score condition: \(67 \geq 75\) is False. Extra-credit condition: \(5 \geq 9\) is False. Since OR requires at least one to be true, and the result is False, the student does not pass.
questions.hint: Check both conditions separately; only one needs to be true for the OR condition to be satisfied.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a compound OR statement given the truth values of its parts
questions.question: Statement P: "There are 10 months in a year." (false). Statement Q: "12 is divisible by 4." (true). What is the truth value of "P OR Q"?

options.label: A
options.text: False

options.label: B
options.text: True

options.label: C
options.text: Cannot be determined

options.label: D
options.text: Neither true nor false

questions.explanation: OR is true when at least one statement is true. Here P is false and Q is true, so P OR Q is true.
questions.hint: 'OR' is true if at least one part is true; it is false only when both parts are false.

questions.learningObjective: Recall the condition under which a compound OR statement is false
questions.question: When is the compound statement 'P OR Q' false?

options.label: A
options.text: When both P and Q are true.

options.label: B
options.text: Whenever P is false, regardless of Q.

options.label: C
options.text: Only when both P and Q are false.

options.label: D
options.text: When at least one of P or Q is false.

questions.explanation: The logical OR (disjunction) is false only in the single case where both individual statements are false; it is true in every other case.
questions.hint: OR is false only when both conditions fail; if either one holds, the whole OR statement is true.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the results of AND and OR for the same pair of truth values
questions.question: If P is false and Q is true, do "P AND Q" and "P OR Q" evaluate to the same truth value or different truth values?

options.label: A
options.text: Different truth values.

options.label: B
options.text: Both are always true regardless of P and Q.

options.label: C
options.text: Both are always false regardless of P and Q.

options.label: D
options.text: The same truth value.

questions.explanation: P AND Q = False. P OR Q = True. These differ, so the results are different.
questions.hint: Evaluate both P AND Q and P OR Q separately for the given truth values, then compare.
